Class FormatAdapters

java.lang.Object
iu.client.FormatAdapters
public final class FormatAdapters extends Object
Date and number conversions by format, shared by the JSON-B provider and the IU binding paths: a date pattern, milliseconds since the epoch, or strict I-JSON for dates, and a decimal pattern for numbers, as JSON-B defines them.

A date type is Date, Calendar, GregorianCalendar, Instant, LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime, OffsetTime, OffsetDateTime, or ZonedDateTime. A date without a zone of its own, Date or Instant, formats in UTC; a Calendar formats in its own zone. A date read without a time is at midnight, and without a zone or offset is in UTC.

    • date

      public static IuJsonAdapter<?> date(Class<?> type, BindingMetadata.Format declared, String configuredPattern, Locale configuredLocale, boolean strict)
      Gets the conversion for a date type.

      A declared format wins over a configured one, even when it declares the default format. The default format is strict I-JSON when configured, and otherwise the built-in conversion.

      Parameters:
      type - date type
      declared - format declared; null if none
      configuredPattern - date pattern configured; null if none
      configuredLocale - locale configured; null for the default locale
      strict - true for strict I-JSON
      Returns:
      conversion; null if nothing is declared or configured

    • strict

      static IuJsonAdapter<Object> strict(Class<?> type)
      Converts a date type as strict I-JSON writes it: Date, Calendar, GregorianCalendar, Instant, LocalDate, and LocalDateTime as an ISO date and time with an offset, seconds included; LocalDate and LocalDateTime in UTC. Other types convert as built in, which writes them that way where they have a date and an offset.

      Reads what it writes, and whatever the built-in conversion reads.

      Parameters:
      type - date type
      Returns:
      conversion
